standfirst: A civil servant inherits a chest of spells and accidentally lands a love potion on the chaebol lawyer who has been cursed for six hundred years. It is a silly premise played with complete conviction, and the leads sell it. These six are for the fated-love-with-jokes register.

picks.why: Same year, same shape, more money. Supernatural obligation, contract logic, chaebol lawyer energy, and a couple whose problem is metaphysical rather than emotional. Difference: My Demon has better production and a much weaker second half, so this one holds together better as a whole.

Fate as paperwork from a previous life. Both build the romance on a debt incurred centuries ago and both make the woman the one who remembers. Difference: it is a melodrama with comic moments rather than a comedy with melodramatic ones, and it hurts more.

The curse-and-destiny template done properly. If the past-life flashbacks were the part you liked, Goblin runs the same idea with real weight and a better score. Difference: the tone is mournful, and the ending will cost you something.

Folklore treated as a working system. Same comfort with charms, spirits and rituals played half straight, half for laughs, and a bickering pair at the centre. Difference: the setting is historical and the horror is real rather than decorative.

Urban fantasy romance with a cursed man at the centre. Same pleasure in a supernatural lead who is rude first and devoted later. Difference: it commits to action sequences, so the pace is a full step faster.

A romance where the obstacle is supernatural admin. Same light touch, same trust in the leads over the lore. Difference: it takes five episodes to find its footing, where Destined with You is working by episode two.

against.title: Hotel del Luna
against.why: The standard fantasy romance recommendation, and much heavier furniture. It is about guilt and the long process of being allowed to leave. This is a comedy about a wooden box.

against.title: Business Proposal
against.why: Paired as the other jTBC-flavoured romcom. Take away the curse and there is no story here at all, which is the opposite of a show built entirely on farce mechanics.

against.title: The Legend of the Blue Sea
against.why: Named for the fated-love-across-lifetimes premise. That show spends its budget on spectacle and its plot on amnesia; Destined with You is small, indoor and character-led.
